name: ODDLPRICE
description: ODDLPRICE returns the price per $100 face value of a bond that has an irregular last coupon period.
tldr: Calculates the price of a security with an odd last coupon period.
syntax: (settlement, maturity, last_interest, rate, yld, redemption, frequency, [basis])

parameters.name: last_interest
parameters.description: Date of the last coupon payment before settlement.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Number of coupon payments per year (1, 2, or 4).

basicExample.description: Price of a bond with an odd last coupon period
basicExample.explanation: Calculates the price of a bond with a last coupon period that is not standard.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/actual basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 1 is common for Treasury bonds.

howItWorks: ODDLPRICE handles bonds where the last coupon period is shorter or longer than a standard coupon period. It adjusts the price for the irregular accrual.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: All dates must be valid Excel dates.
Last interest date must be before maturity but after the issue date.

commonErrors.fix: Verify all inputs and date order.
Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ODDLPRICE works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is an odd last coupon period?
faq.answer: It is a final coupon period that is not a standard length because the bond matures on an off-cycle date.

faq.question: When is ODDLPRICE used?
faq.answer: It is used for bonds that mature on a date that does not align with the coupon schedule.
